column2: Each prompt stands alone and nothing carries over between interactions; even a long context window has a start and an end. (§1.1)
Keeps a working context that evolves over time; its current state results from earlier events and shapes later ones. (§1.1)

column1: Chatbot vs. agent: the weekly briefing
column2: A chatbot needs fresh data pasted each week and can't recall last week's answer; an agent compares against the prior state it recorded. (§1.1)
Records outcomes so the next session starts knowing today's decisions; it is what makes persistence meaningful. (§1.3)
A framework system prompt resets each session; Claw identity files exist outside any conversation and load fresh every session. (§1.3.1)
Loading whole files every session costs more tokens than retrieving RAG chunks, but the agent always has its complete identity. (§1.3.1)
Values and decision priorities: communication, value conflicts, hard limits, and ambiguity handling. Changes rarely. (§3.2)
Procedures: session initialization, confirmation gates, group behavior, and memory governance rules. (§3.3)
Persistent user context and calibration: name, timezone, role, expertise, preferences, and topics to avoid raising. (§3.4)
Curated, dated, durable facts likely to affect decisions weeks or months later; maintained deliberately, not auto-generated. (§3.5)
memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md: a model-written session summary of decisions, tool calls, and open items. Today's and yesterday's load by default. (§2.7)
Moving a durable fact from daily logs into MEMORY.md, by user instruction, agent proposal with confirmation, or scheduled review. (§3.5)
Outdated facts the model applies with full confidence, producing answers that are precisely wrong rather than vaguely generic. (§2.7)
An injected false MEMORY.md entry loads into every later session. Restrict memory writes to direct user instructions and confirmed facts. (§2.7)
Session history carries context within one session; the memory log carries what should outlast it. (§4.4)
